- When sentiment is consistently high (>0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, it often overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1.2x recent high.
- In low sentiment (≤0.3) periods, model underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast mean to compensate for downward bias.
- Model frequently overpredicts 30-day horizon after recent price spikes; apply 10–15% downward adjustment if last 3 days show >0.8 sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows rising trend, model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast to account for momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast by averaging last 3 values before final output.
